rv.q: Ayckbourn's comic masterwork receives a sterling revival that captures both the playwright's surgical wit and his underlying compassion for his flawed characters.
What emerges is a portrait of sexual frustration and romantic delusion so comprehensive and convincing that you feel as if you've been living with these people for years.
This middle play of Ayckbourn's trilogy works best as a standalone piece, with its clever staging of romantic chaos in real time.
The Norman Conquests: Table Manners is a marvel of construction and characterization that demonstrates Ayckbourn's mastery of the well-made play.
This is farce of the highest caliber, with every line and every moment calculated to maximum comic effect.
And the captivating actors, who won this year’s Award for Outstanding Ensemble, are perfectly irresistible.
